Subject: NexaBio - Order Form v3 redlines + runbook witness request

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. Attached is our redlined Order Form (v3) and a short list of runbook/witness asks from our security and compliance team. High-level asks:

- Clarify license boundary language in Section 2.1 (we want explicit operator access carveouts for customer-managed private deployments)
- Request a witness session for the runbook that demonstrates snapshot + restore and operator handover (remote acceptable)
- Evidence for custody/escrow-lite: prefer a sealed snapshot + notarized transfer receipt or a third-party custodian; open to Redwood proposals

Can you confirm: (a) whether Redwood can accept our redlines by next week, (b) expected timeline for the witness session, and (c) what artifacts you’ll provide (runbook extract, signed order form, attestation)?

I attached: Nexa_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf and a short runbook export we were shown on the demo.

Thanks,
Eugene Park
Head of Procurement, NexaBio

Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NexaBio - Order Form v3 redlines + runbook witness request

Eugene — thanks for the detailed packet and clear asks. We can take the following near-term approach:

1) License boundary: we can accept your operator-access carveout in principle but need a short, alternative clause to replace the current Section 2.1 wording. I’ve looped in Marissa from Legal to draft wording that balances our IP residency commitments with your operational requirements.

2) Witness session: remote witness is fine. We can run a 45–60 minute session (screen-share + live snapshot/restore) and provide the runbook extract you need. Proposed windows: week of Sep 6 (PDT) or week of Sep 13 (PDT). Please indicate preferences.

3) Escrow-lite / sealed snapshot: Redwood does not have an external escrow custodian pre-contracted for every deal, but we can support a sealed snapshot export with notarized checksums plus an audited transfer receipt. We can also integrate a third-party custodian if you require it; there may be an additional cost and a short procurement step.

I’m attaching a redline-summary.xlsx that calls out items we believe are straightforward vs items needing legal signoff. I’ll coordinate the legal language with Marissa and return with proposed clause alternatives by EOD Tue.

Next steps: can your team confirm preferred witness week and whether remote-only is acceptable? Also confirm a primary signatory for DocuSign once we finalize the Order Form.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Ops — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

[Attachment: redline-summary.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Kimberly / Vanessa —

I reviewed the redlines. Summary and suggested legal edits below (inline to your spreadsheet and attached as a small text exhibit):

- Section 2.1 (License scope): propose alternate language that limits operator access to ephemeral console sessions tied to a documented witness event and explicitly prohibits moving customer data outside the agreed region. This preserves Redwood IP and addresses NexaBio’s operational test needs.

- Exhibit F (Runbook / Witness): recommend a short Exhibit F that outlines witness scope (snapshot creation, hash verification, restore verification, operator credential handover steps) and the artefacts we will provide (MD5/SHA256 checksums, runbook excerpt, video recording if permitted).

- Escrow-lite: accept sealed snapshot + notarized transfer receipt as an acceptable path. If NexaBio insists on a third-party escrow custodian we’ll propose a standardized addendum with a small fee and SLA for retrieval.

I attached legal-proposed-clause.txt with suggested replacement text for Section 2.1 and a draft Exhibit F template. If NexaBio signs off on the Exhibit F scope, Legal is comfortable rolling this into the Order Form as an Annex rather than a full MSA amendment.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

[Attachment: legal-proposed-clause.txt (text)]
